item.title: China to continue hydrological information sharing with Nepal to support disaster response
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-03
China to continue hydrological information sharing with Nepal to support disaster response BEIJING, Sept. 2 (Xinhua) -- China will continue to share information on barrier lake risks, glacial lake risks and emergency hydrological monitoring with Nepal to support disaster rescue and relief efforts, an official with the Ministry of Water Resources said Wednesday. A fast-moving chain mudslide, triggered by a high-altitude glacier collapse in Nepal, struck Gyirong Port on the China-Nepal border in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region on Aug. 26, causing severe damage to the port and destroying hydrological monitoring facilities. As of Wednesday noon, 21 people had been confirmed dead and 541 others remained missing, according to the latest update from the Xizang regional government. The disaster-hit area poses significant challenges for hydrological monitoring, as it is surrounded by high mountains, deep valleys and numerous glaciers and glacial lakes, the ministry said. China's emergency hydrological monitoring team is working to restore the damaged monitoring stations, establish an early warning system, and closely monitor key risk areas. It is also continuing to share hydrological monitoring information with Nepal. The ministry is now providing Nepal with daily updates on the development of a barrier lake above the Gyirong Port, cascading risks associated with the Cuojian River impact crater in Nepal, glacial lake risks in the Gyirong Zangbo River basin, the development and risk forecasts of new barrier lakes, and emergency hydrological monitoring. The geological conditions in the Gyirong disaster-hit area remain highly unstable, with risks of further landslides, rockfalls and other secondary hazards, the ministry warned. The large number of glacial lakes in the surrounding area is also adding to the uncertainty. The timely information provided by the ministry offers Nepal much-needed technical support, helping its authorities carry out rescue and emergency response efforts, evacuate residents in a timely manner and reduce casualties, the ministry said. Looking ahead, China will work with Nepal to promote the signing of an agreement on hydrological information sharing for transboundary rivers and establish a regular cooperation mechanism, with the aim of jointly strengthening disaster prevention and mitigation, it added. item.title: China opposes using G20 to hype so-called "economic imbalances": commerce ministry
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-03
China opposes using G20 to hype so-called "economic imbalances": commerce ministry BEIJING, Sept. 3 (Xinhua) -- China's Ministry of Commerce on Thursday voiced strong opposition to the use of multilateral platforms such as the G20 to hype so-called "economic imbalances" and "overcapacity." Spokesperson Huang Ling made the remarks in response to a question about recent comments by U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent concerning China. Such rhetoric is essentially a cover for protectionism and an excuse to pressure and restrain China, Huang said. "This will only disrupt global trade and economic order and undermine the sound development of the world economy," she added. Huang called on all countries to uphold multilateralism, enhance policy communication and coordination, expand openness and cooperation, and jointly keep global industrial and supply chains stable and smooth to achieve mutually beneficial outcomes. item.title: Traditional warning insufficient, remote sensing of slopes needed as ice-rock avalanche risks on the rise: intl experts
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-03
Traditional warning insufficient, remote sensing of slopes needed as ice-rock avalanche risks on the rise: intl experts This photo taken on Aug. 26, 2026 shows a view of the mudslide-hit area. Three people had been killed and 265 others remained missing as of 8 p.m. Wednesday after a mudslide struck Gyirong port along the China-Nepal border in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region, officials said. (Xinhua) The devastating mudslide that swept from Nepal's Mount Langtang Lirung to China's Xizang Autonomous Region in minutes highlights the growing challenge of detecting and warning against fast-moving ice-rock avalanche disasters in the Himalayas, international experts told the Global Times, warning that such events could become more frequent as glaciers and permafrost destabilize under a warming climate. An ice-rock avalanche originating from a high-mountain glacier in Nepal triggered the disaster that struck Gyirong Port on August 26, according to an assessment by Chinese authorities. A glacier on the north slope of Mount Langtang Lirung fractured at an altitude of about 5,200 meters, sending an avalanche rapidly down to around 4,000 meters, where it scoured the mountainside and transformed into a massive debris flow. The flow traveled about 22 kilometers before reaching Gyirong Port, at an altitude of around 1,800 meters, Xinhua News Agency reported. The disaster was exceptionally rapid. The debris flow reached the port only about six to seven minutes after the initial collapse, according to researchers cited by Xinhua. Jakob Steiner, a geoscientist at the University of Graz in Austria, told the Global Times that satellite imagery and the depth of the scar indicate that the event may have begun with a bedrock failure, rather than instability of the glacier itself. "The ice just added material and likely contributed to the flood wave and extent," Steiner said Steiner also stressed that longer-term environmental changes and instability of the slope were likely more important than the short-term melting of snow and ice observed before the collapse. The recent melt may have acted as the final trigger, he said, while the slope could otherwise have failed somewhat later. Kristen Cook, a geomorphologist at the Institute of Earth Science at Grenoble Alpes University in France, similarly told the Global Times that the bedrock collapsed first. Given the relatively small size of the glacier compared with the rock mass involved, she said, glacial instability was unlikely to have had a major influence on the initial failure. Cook said the slope's long-term stability would have been influenced by a combination of climate warming, geological processes and tectonic activity, although research into these factors is still underway. The event also challenges conventional classifications of high-mountain disasters, according to the experts. The Langtang Lirung event was very similar to the deadly 2021 Chamoli disaster in India's Uttarakhand, Cook said, rejecting descriptions of the August 26 event as a glacial lake outburst flood, or GLOF, she noted. "It was a rock/ice avalanche that continued flowing down the valley after the initial collapse," she said, adding that there was no initial damming and breaching involved in the event itself. The distinction is important for disaster preparedness because a destructive flood-like event can occur without a glacial lake, Cook said. Both experts mentioned the 2021 catastrophic mass flow descended into valleys in Chamoli of Uttarakhand state in India, causing widespread devastation and severely damaging two hydropower projects. Over 200 people were killed or missing. Steiner identified Chamoli as the closest comparison to the Langtang Lirung event in terms of the processes involved, although the volumes and terrain differed. The disaster therefore underscores the need to broaden hazard assessments beyond conventional GLOFs and other relatively familiar glacier-related hazards, experts said. The biggest challenge, however, may be detecting such events early enough before they happen. Cook said there are currently no operational early-warning systems based on seismological monitoring for this type of event, while satellite-based early-warning systems are also not yet widely operational. Hydrological monitoring has its own limitations. Instruments installed alongside rivers can be destroyed by the very floods they are supposed to detect. Even when they survive long enough to record the beginning of a flood, they may not be able to determine its magnitude quickly enough to provide useful information to downstream communities, Cook said. Steiner said detection is "very tricky," noting that even when a potentially dangerous signal is detected, experts still need to interpret it. Excessive reliance on raw signals could otherwise generate too many false alarms. Instead, analyzing satellite imagery for concerning patterns before a collapse may prove more useful, he said. Cook advocated developing automated slope-deformation monitoring using remote sensing, which could provide a more practical way to identify unstable slopes in remote high-altitude terrain. For Steiner, this disaster should not be regarded as an isolated extreme event. "We unfortunately definitely see this as an emerging pattern," he said. "It is not an isolated event any more and we need to be prepared to see it more often." Cook offered a more nuanced assessment. While the Langtang Lirung event was extremely large, she expected more rock/ice avalanche-related flood cascades across High Mountain Asia in the future, although most would likely be considerably smaller. She noted that even a collapse 100 times smaller than the Langtang Lirung event could potentially generate a disastrous flood, citing the 2023 mudflow in Shovi, Georgia, as an example. "The key is to develop automated slope deformation monitoring using remote sensing," Cook said. The combination of high-altitude source areas, steep terrain, rapid transformation and extremely short warning windows means that conventional disaster-warning approaches may not be sufficient, experts said. item.title: Global resonance of Xi's selfless commitment to the people
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-03
Global resonance of Xi's selfless commitment to the people Chinese President Xi Jinping holds talks with Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, Aug. 31, 2026. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi) On the morning of August 31, during talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping, Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov expressed admiration for the remarkable development achievements China has made under the leadership of Xi, and voiced willingness to learn from China's experience in state governance, particularly Xi's commitment to the people, as embodied in his words, "I will fully commit to the people and never fail them." In March 2019, during his state visit to Italy, Xi met with Roberto Fico, then president of the Italian Chamber of Deputies. Fico asked Xi, "What did you feel when you were elected Chinese president?" "Governing such a huge country requires a strong sense of responsibility and hard work," said Xi. "For the good of my people, I will put aside my own well-being. I am willing to be selfless and devote myself to China's development." Xi has spoken of this conviction on multiple occasions. During his trip to the United States in November, 2023, Xi recalled in a speech at a welcome dinner hosted by friendly organizations that, before turning 16, he was in a village in northern Shaanxi Province, where he lived and farmed with villagers, and knew about their worries and needs. He said that, over the past half-century, he had always felt confident and strong when staying with the people. “Serving the people selflessly and living up to their expectations is my lifelong commitment,” he said. Xi not only keeps in mind major issues concerning the national economy and people's livelihood, but also cares about the everyday concerns of ordinary people. During his local inspection tours, Xi chatted with local residents about their daily lives and household finances, felt the quilts on their beds to make sure they stay warm, lifted the lids of cooking pots to see whether they eat well, asked about whether they had rich cultural and spiritual lives, and attached great importance to the healthy development of young people. From securing a decisive victory in poverty alleviation to comprehensively advancing rural revitalization, from achieving a moderately prosperous society in all respects to marching toward common prosperity, Chinese Communists in the new era have borne in mind thecountry'smostfundamentalinterests — ensuring that the people live happy lives. They have devoted themselves wholeheartedly to this cause, forged ahead undauntedly to achieve it, and made persistent efforts to bring it to fruition. People's well-being is of utmost importance in Chinese modernization. China's development achievements vividly demonstrate its people-centered development philosophy. China now has the world's largest education, social security and healthcare systems, while achieving historic strides in making education universally available. During the 14th Five-Year Plan period, average life expectancy in China rose to 79.25 years, more than 12 million new urban jobs were created each year on average, and direct settlement of cross-provincial medical expenses benefited 560 million medical visits nationwide. In the opening year of the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-30) period, China's head-of-state diplomacy has witnessed one highlight after another, with more and more foreign leaders seeking inspiration from China's governance model for their own development. During his state visit to China, Mozambican President Daniel Francisco Chapo made a special trip to Banyan Village of Huzhu Tu Autonomous County in northwest China's Qinghai Province, where Xi Jinping visited during an inspection tour in 2016. "Seeing is believing. With China's targeted poverty alleviation policies effectively implemented, Banyan Village has undergone tremendous changes, which is truly inspiring." Chapo said, adding that the experience is also exemplary for the world. At the entrance of Yucun Village in Anji County, east China’s Zhejiang Province, Thongloun Sisoulith, General Secretary of the Lao People's Revolutionary Party Central Committee and Lao President, took a photo of the inscription carved on a boulder, which reads,"lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets." After hearing a briefing on the "Green Rural Revival Program" — which was initiated in June 2003 by Xi, then secretary of the CPC Zhejiang Provincial Committee, with a plan to renovate about 10,000 incorporated villages in five years and transform about 1,000 central villages among them into examples of moderate prosperity in all respects — Thongloun lauded the program as remarkable for creating countless beautiful villages. During Xi’s visit to Kyrgyzstan, how to further improve people's well-being remains a key concern for him. "Pursuing high-quality cooperation on the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway, a transportation artery carrying the region's aspirations for development," "further promoting personnel exchanges and strengthening cooperation in such areas as youth, media, tourism, sports, and medical care, and at subnational levels," and "steadily consolidating the societal foundation of and popular support for China-Kyrgyzstan friendship" — these are among the priorities highlighted by Xi. "The people's aspiration for a better life is what we are striving for." This deep commitment to the people is reflected in practice, offers inspiration for the future, and allows the international community to gain a deeper appreciation of the CPC's people-centered governance philosophy and its strong sense of mission and responsibility. "I will fully commit to the people and never fail them." This is not merely a powerful pledge, but a commitment translated into concrete action. The vision of enabling hundreds of millions of people to live better lives is resonating more widely around the world. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: Xi's four-point proposal offers Chinese solution for Mideast peace, stability: Chinese FM
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-03
Xi's four-point proposal offers Chinese solution for Mideast peace, stability: Chinese FM BEIJING, Sept. 3 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping's four-point proposal on building a new security architecture in the Middle East once again offers a Chinese solution for achieving long-term peace and stability in the region, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi has said. Wang, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, made the remarks while briefing reporters on the conclusion of Xi's attendance at the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Bishkek Summit and state visits to Kyrgyzstan and Egypt. Xi put forward the proposal in his talks with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, calling for unleashing internal drivers, advancing an integrated approach, cementing development foundation, and enhancing international coordination. International observers believe that Xi's proposal has offered a viable path toward resolving the Middle East's security dilemma, Wang said. During the visit, Xi had in-depth exchanges with leaders of various countries on world affairs and hotspot issues, speaking up for peace and standing up for justice, said Wang. On the sidelines of the Bishkek summit, Xi held separate meetings with Russian President Vladimir Putin, Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Mongolian President Ukhnaa Khurelsukh. Xi and Putin agreed to deepen China-Russia comprehensive strategic coordination, advance reform of global governance, promote a multipolar world, and jointly safeguard world peace, stability and development, Wang noted. Guided by Xi Jinping Thought on Diplomacy, China has been exploring a distinctly Chinese approach to resolving hotspot issues, Wang said, adding that no matter how complex the disputes or how intense the conflicts, China will always stand firmly on the side of peace and dialogue and on the right side of history. item.title: Xi, Peng Liyuan visit Grand Egyptian Museum
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-03
Xi, Peng Liyuan visit Grand Egyptian Museum Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan, accompanied by Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi and his wife Entissar El-Sisi, tour the Grand Egyptian Museum in Giza, Egypt, Sept. 2, 2026. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi) CAIRO, Sept. 2 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife, Peng Liyuan, visited on Wednesday the Grand Egyptian Museum accompanied by Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi and his wife. The two heads of state and their spouses took in the exquisite and imposing stone carvings and inscribed stone pillars. They then gazed out at the pyramids from the museum's observation deck. Entering the Tutankhamun exhibition hall, the two presidents viewed such prized treasures as the pharaoh's throne, the golden mask and royal chariots. Noting that China and Egypt are both ancient civilizations and countries rich in World Heritage sites, Xi said that across time and space, the two civilizations have been reaching out to each other, adding new chapters of everlasting friendship between the two peoples. Xi called on both sides to uphold the vision of civilization based on equality, mutual learning, dialogue and inclusiveness, and implement the Global Civilization Initiative. He also urged the two countries to promote the inclusive coexistence and mutual learning among different civilizations, and pool greater strength from civilizations to advance the building of a community with a shared future for humanity. Sisi thanked Xi for extending congratulations on the opening of the museum last year. He said the ancient Egyptian and Chinese civilizations share the qualities of openness, inclusiveness and harmonious coexistence amid diversity, which closely aligns with the vision of the Global Civilization Initiative proposed by Xi. The Egyptian side stands ready to work with China to step up people-to-people and cultural exchanges, promote mutual learning among civilizations, and make the world more harmonious and inclusive, Sisi said. item.title: Xi calls for deepening China-Egypt cooperation, raises Mideast proposal
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-03
Xi calls for deepening China-Egypt cooperation, raises Mideast proposal Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan pose for a group photo with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi and his wife Entissar El-Sisi in Cairo, Egypt, Sept. 2, 2026. Xi held talks with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi in Cairo on Wednesday. (Xinhua/Yin Bogu) CAIRO, Sept. 2 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Wednesday called on China and Egypt to support each other, deepen cooperation, and continue advancing the building of a China-Egypt community with a shared future amid a turbulent international and regional landscape. Xi made the remarks during his talks with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, while emphasizing China's support for regional countries in building a new security architecture in the Middle East via upholding a vision of common, comprehensive, cooperative and sustainable security. ENHANCING BILATERAL EXCHANGES, COOPERATION Noting that Egypt was the first Arab and African nation to establish diplomatic ties with the People's Republic of China in 1956, Xi said that the older-generation leaders of the two countries led their peoples in striving side by side for national independence and against imperialism and colonialism, forging an unbreakable bond of friendship. Over the past seven decades, China-Egypt relations have weathered challenges and developed distinctive features of equality and mutual trust, friendship and mutual learning, solidarity and mutual support, as well as win-win cooperation, he said. Xi said the China-Egypt comprehensive strategic partnership has achieved leapfrog development in recent years under the guidance of the two heads of state. The two sides share similar views and have closely aligned strategies in pursuing development and revitalization, improving people's well-being, and upholding international fairness and justice, he added. Xi emphasized that China and Egypt should firmly support each other, maintain the momentum of high-level exchanges, enhance exchanges and cooperation in all fields and at all levels, and strengthen exchanges and mutual learning on governance experience. Xi said the two sides should promote mutually beneficial cooperation, better align their development strategies, tap the potential for cooperation in traditional fields such as infrastructure development, power, agriculture and communications technology, and foster new highlights of cooperation in green energy, electric vehicles, aerospace, the digital economy and modern agricultural technology. The two sides should promote people-to-people exchanges, comprehensively expand exchanges and cooperation in culture, education, science and technology, health, sports and other fields, and facilitate personnel exchanges and enhance people-to-people bonds, Xi said. The two sides should strengthen security cooperation, jointly combat transnational crime, deepen international cooperation in anti-corruption, firmly support each other's anti-terror efforts, and safeguard their common security, Xi said. The two sides should strengthen multilateral collaboration, further enhance coordination and cooperation on multilateral platforms such as the United Nations and the BRICS, jointly promote the development of the China-Arab States Cooperation Forum and the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation, jointly oppose unilateralism and acts of bullying, and promote a more just and equitable global governance system, Xi said. For his part, Sisi welcomed Xi's historic state visit to Egypt on the occasion of the 70th anniversary of diplomatic ties between the two countries. Sisi said that since the establishment of diplomatic relations, bilateral ties have developed in a sound and steady manner, and cooperation across various fields has yielded fruitful results. Egypt firmly adheres to the one-China principle and is committed to further advancing the Egypt-China comprehensive strategic partnership, Sisi added. Egypt is ready to work with China to deepen cooperation in trade and investment, manufacturing, infrastructure development, finance, science and technology, and new energy, strengthen military and security exchanges, and promote closer people-to-people exchanges, so as to benefit the two peoples and contribute to regional development and prosperity, Sisi said. Sisi said China, as a permanent member of the UN Security Council, plays an important and constructive role in international affairs. Egypt is ready to strengthen coordination with China at multilateral platforms, jointly address global challenges, and work together to uphold international fairness and justice, he added. The two heads of state jointly witnessed the signing of multiple cooperation documents on Belt and Road cooperation, artificial intelligence, economic and trade, and industrial and supply chain cooperation. The two sides also issued a joint statement on further deepening their comprehensive strategic partnership, and signed more than 20 cooperation documents covering such areas as digital economy, science and technology, education, and transportation. NEW REGIONAL SECURITY ARCHITECTURE In the talks, Xi raised a four-point proposal on building a new security architecture in the Middle East, saying that China supports countries in the region in developing good-neighborly and friendly relations. To promote common security in the region, Xi said that efforts should be made to foster the internal driving force for common security in the region. People in the Middle East should remain masters of their own affairs, and external interference should be rejected, Xi said, noting that China supports regional countries in strengthening dialogue on peace and security, exploring the building of a new security architecture for the Middle East, and taking their future into their own hands. Xi said that a comprehensive approach should be adopted to advance common security in the region and that given the multiple hotspots in the Middle East and their close interconnections, comprehensive solutions should be pursued. The Palestinian issue remains at the core of the Middle East question and should never be overlooked or marginalized, he added. The foundation for common security should be strengthened through development, Xi said, noting that lasting peace and stability in the Middle East fundamentally depend on development. China stands ready to work with Middle East countries to safeguard the security of international shipping lanes, advance development cooperation, promote the convergence of interests of regional countries, gradually enhance mutual trust, and eliminate the root causes of the conflict, he said. Xi urged that international coordination for common security in the region should be strengthened, and the UN Charter and international law should serve as the fundamental principles for handling Middle East affairs. The international community, especially external powers, should abandon double standards in the Middle East, respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of regional countries, and safeguard regional peace and stability, Xi added. He also urged support for the United Nations' effective role in Middle East affairs. Sisi said that Egypt highly appreciates China's consistent, objective, and impartial stance on the Middle East question, noting that Egypt is committed to promoting de-escalation in the region, resolving conflicts and differences through political means, and advancing regional security and development. Egypt stands ready to continue strengthening coordination with China to ease tensions in the Middle East, safeguard regional stability, and explore a regional security architecture, Sisi said. During the visit, Xi held talks with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi. item.title: Xi returns to Beijing after SCO summit, state visits to Kyrgyzstan, Egypt
item.description:

Xi returns to Beijing after SCO summit, state visits to Kyrgyzstan, Egypt (Xinhua) 11:10, September 03, 2026
BEIJING, Sept. 3 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping returned to Beijing on Thursday after attending the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Summit 2026 in Bishkek, and concluding his state visits to Kyrgyzstan and Egypt. Xi's entourage, including his wife Peng Liyuan, Cai Qi, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and director of the General Office of the CPC Central Committee, and Wang Yi, a member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Chinese foreign minister, returned on the same flight.
